_comment: #475/#492. `neighborhoods` is informational - BuildingTemplateLibraryImporter reads it for one
log line and nothing matches against it. It lists exactly the neighborhoods some template
admits, spelled as python/data/sf_analysis_neighborhoods.geojson spells them: the slashes in
"Sunset/Parkside" and the whole of "South of Market" are the match key the bake passes
through verbatim. (A slashed name is no longer a problem for the importer either - it
percent-encodes the generated asset's FILE NAME via AssetFileName.Encode while keeping the
slashed string as the lookup key. #464.)
`districtTemplateWeights` is load-bearing (#343). Two templates admit one neighborhood on
purpose - a shopfront cannot share floor 0 with a garage and a door, and the schema has no way
to say 'these two placements are mutually exclusive' inside one template - so the split has to
happen at template selection. Without weights TryMatch's tie-break is uniform and every second
building in the Victorian belt, or in the Mission, would be a shop.
EVERY ROW ALSO LISTS trivial_window AT 0. It is the bundled MVP sample (README): its
compatibility.neighborhoods is empty, which means it admits every building in the city, so it
competed in every district. #475 could only thin it - NeighborhoodTemplateWeights.WeightFor
treated an authored 0 as 'unset' and fell back to 1, leaving the sample at ~1 building in 14
with no way to exclude it. WeightFor now takes 0 literally (#492), so a district can switch a
template off. Two consequences worth knowing: (1) presence in the list is the signal, and
JsonUtility maps a MISSING "weight" field to 0, so omit the whole entry rather than the
number when you mean 'compete at the default' - the importer logs every zero it reads;
(2) this only helps where a district row exists. In a neighborhood no template admits,
trivial_window is still the ONLY match and still wins, weights or not. Giving the sample a
real compatibility is the fix for that, and it would change what the README documents, so it
was left alone.
